blocks.text: "A 34-week fetus has an EFW on the 7th centile. What would you do?"
"An estimated fetal weight on the 7th centile indicates that the fetus is small for gestational age. However, this does not automatically establish fetal growth restriction."
"I would first confirm that the gestational age is accurate and review previous ultrasound measurements to assess the growth trajectory."

"I would assess fetal biometry, particularly abdominal circumference, as well as amniotic fluid and umbilical artery Doppler. Depending on the gestational age and clinical circumstances, I would also consider MCA Doppler, CTG and other fetal surveillance."
"I would assess the mother for hypertension and evidence of pre-eclampsia and review other maternal risk factors."

"If the fetus is tracking appropriately with normal Dopplers and no evidence of compromise, it may represent a constitutionally small fetus and can be monitored appropriately. If there is evidence of abnormal growth trajectory, placental insufficiency or fetal compromise, I would manage this as suspected fetal growth restriction with specialist input and plan delivery according to the gestational age and fetal and maternal condition."
